title: KVCache phantom-prefetch congestion and reconciliation runbook
creator: Aisha Raman
description: Follow-up for a capacity incident where speculative prefetches created transient 'phantom' entries that blocked eviction scoring, drove slab fragmentation, and led to a cascade of eviction backpressure across hosts. This ticket captures the immediate mitigations, telemetry gaps, and long-term reconciliations to prevent recurrence.
incident_summary: Between 2026-02-24 03:12 and 2026-02-24 03:46 UTC, a regional capacity degradation was observed on serving nodes. Hosts experienced memory growth without corresponding live-key traffic, eviction windows closed unexpectedly, and CPU latencies spiked due to compaction churn. Root cause analysis indicates an interaction between speculative prefetch insertion and our eviction scoring decay logic that allowed low-value prefetch entries to persist and artificially inflate active set size.
root_cause: A re-entrant prefetch code path inserted entries with default retention flags; these entries were incorrectly treated as resident for eviction score decay. Under load, the prefetch rate exceeded the decay/eviction throughput, producing a growing reservoir of cold entries that were evaluated as live. Combined with a slab compaction race (PR #8791) this produced fragmentation and prolonged eviction stalls.
timeline: 2026-02-24 03:12 UTC - First alert: per-host free memory dropping below threshold in eu-west-1
2026-02-24 03:18 UTC - Autoscaling triggered but hosts still reported high eviction latencies
2026-02-24 03:25 UTC - On-call throttled prefetch feature via dynamic config (rollout-ctl) — temporary relief noted
2026-02-24 03:33 UTC - Emergency rollback of recent prefetch kernel (deploy r2.10.13) started
2026-02-24 03:46 UTC - Memory trend reversed, eviction latencies returned to baseline
2026-02-24 04:20 UTC - Incident declared mitigated and postmortem initiated
mitigations: Immediate: roll back speculative prefetch flag to disabled in eu-west-1 via rollout-ctl (on-call)
Immediate: apply temporary prefetch rate cap at 5 req/s per core to reduce insertion pressure
Short-term: add a volatile bit to prefetch entries so they are excluded from eviction score decay and persistent pinning
Short-term: add a circuit-breaker config to disable speculative prefetch when host free memory < 12%
Monitoring: create dashboard tile 'kvcache:prefetch-insert-rate vs eviction-delay' and an alert for sustained insert:evict ratio > 2
long_term_actions: Change prefetch insertion to mark entries as 'probationary' + TTL 30s and exclude from prefetched-hit metrics until first access (owner: Marco, estimate: 5)
Rewrite eviction-score decay to explicitly ignore probationary/volatile entries and add unit tests covering decay under concurrent insertion (owner: Elena Park, estimate: 8)
Introduce per-namespace prefetch quotas and a token-bucket backed throttler that can be tuned per-customer workload (owner: SRE team, estimate: 8)
Address slab compaction race by serializing compact operations per-slab with an opportunistic backoff; include microbenchmarks to validate latency cost (owner: Arun Patel, estimate: 5)
Expand incident runbook: add step to check 'prefetch-insert:evict' ratio and how to toggle dynamic-config flags (owner: on-call docs, estimate: 2)
Post-release: schedule a canary that enables probationary prefetch behavior behind a feature flag and measure memory trends over 48h (owner: Platform QA, estimate: 3)
Add automated continuous-eval that runs prefix-cache eviction stress test in CI to detect regressions on insertion/decay paths (owner: CI team, estimate: 5)
immediate_action_items: (A) Feature-flag rollback confirmation: ensure rollback was applied cluster-wide and document scope (owner: on-call, done)
(B) Postmortem draft + timeline entry posted to #incidents with links to dashboards (owner: Aisha Raman, done)
(C) Create 'prefetch:inserted/evicted' counter and wire into existing cost dashboard (owner: Marco Villanueva, in progress)
(D) Hotfix: add volatile bit handling to eviction loop to short-circuit probationary entries (owner: Marco, in review, PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving/pull/9182)
(E) Run a cross-team sanity sweep to ensure no other code paths insert untagged prefetch entries (owner: Engineering leads, todo)
(F) Update rollback runbook with the exact rollout-ctl commands used and add post-rollback verification steps (owner: SRE, todo)
observability_gaps: No metric existed for 'prefetch_entry_type' so we could not distinguish user-insert from speculative-insert in real time
Eviction delay alerts used per-host moving averages which masked host-level oscillation during compaction
Lack of correlation tile between prefetch rate and slab-fragmentation metrics
validation_plan: Unit + integration tests to assert probationary entries are not counted in eviction score and are cleared after TTL
Canary rollout: enable probationary prefetch on 1% of traffic for 72 hours and monitor 'mem-reservation' and 'eviction-delay' metrics
Load test: simulate 10k/sec prefetch rate in staging and validate no >10% increase in eviction latency over baseline
notes: Decision: probationary TTL default set to 30s after cross-team discussion; value chosen to balance short-term speculative value vs memory pressure
Trade-off: marking entries probationary will hide some perf wins for cold-starts but prevents long tail memory growth — acceptable for production SLOs
Follow-up: investigate adding a tiny 'utility score' to prefetch candidates to avoid prefetching very low-value keys
